stripped_sentences: She announced that the bloc was releasing 710 million euros for people hit by crises, natural disasters or conflict, most of it for Africa

failed_claims.claim: Ursula von der Leyen announced on Saturday that the EU was releasing 710 million euros, including 380 million for sub-Saharan Africa and 252 million from the emergency reserve, with part of the package for Ukraine's winter.
failed_claims.episode_span: She announced that the bloc was releasing 710 million euros for people hit by crises, natural disasters or conflict, most of it for Africa
failed_claims.supporting_quote: European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen announced Saturday the bloc was releasing 710 million euros to help people hit by crises, natural disasters or conflict, most of it for Africa.

claims.claim: Belfast's Court of Appeal overturned a ban late on Saturday and the Orange Order parade down Garvaghy Road was due at 8am on Sunday.
claims.episode_span: Late on Saturday, Belfast's Court of Appeal overturned a High Court injunction and allowed the Orange Order to parade down the Garvaghy Road in Portadown, County Armagh, at 8am on Sunday.
claims.source_title: Loyalist parade in Northern Ireland given go-ahead as almost 30-year ban overturned
claims.supporting_quote: Amid fears the march could unleash fresh sectarian violence, the Orange Order parade down the Garvaghy Road is due to take place at 8am on Sunday, and follows a legal back-and-forth in recent days.

claims.claim: Thirty-five Orange Order members are to march the largely nationalist Garvaghy Road for the first time in 28 years after a Friday Parades Commission grant, a route refused since 1998.
claims.episode_span: 35 members are to walk the largely nationalist road for the first time in 28 years, after the Parades Commission on Friday granted an application it had refused since 1998.
claims.source_title: Orange Order to march down Garvaghy Road for first time in almost 30 years
claims.supporting_quote: 35 members of the Orange Order are to march down the Garvaghy Road, a largely nationalist area in Portadown, Co Armagh, this morning for the first time in 28 years.

claims.claim: Judge Patricia Smyth suspended the parade after a five-hour hearing and urged sides to step back from the abyss, citing a risk of escalation.
claims.episode_span: Judge Patricia Smyth suspended the parade, said the long-running dispute had the potential to escalate across Northern Ireland, and urged all sides to step back from the abyss.
claims.source_title: Loyalist parade in Northern Ireland given go-ahead as almost 30-year ban overturned
claims.supporting_quote: Smyth had urged all sides to “step back from the abyss” and take responsible decisions for “the sake of everyone in Northern Ireland”.

claims.claim: At 11.30pm Judge Siobhan Keegan said the High Court judge had erred in law.
claims.episode_span: At 11.30pm Judge Siobhan Keegan said the High Court judge had erred in law
claims.source_title: Loyalist parade in Northern Ireland given go-ahead as almost 30-year ban overturned
claims.supporting_quote: But at 11.30pm on Saturday, at a sitting of the court of appeals, Judge Siobhan Keegan said the high court judge who granted the injunction against the march had “unfortunately erred in law”.

claims.claim: Judge Michael Humphreys dismissed a fresh overnight application, finding the Parades Commission had weighed the evidence and that the legal threshold to strike down its decision was not met.
claims.episode_span: Judge Michael Humphreys dismissed a fresh application, saying the commission had taken evidence, weighed the issues and reached a reasoned decision, and that the threshold for striking it down had not been met.
claims.source_title: Loyalist parade in Northern Ireland given go-ahead as almost 30-year ban overturned
claims.supporting_quote: “The picture painted here is of a public body which took evidence from the relevant sources, weighed up the key issues which were in play and arrived at a reasoned decision,” he said.

claims.claim: The Police Service of Northern Ireland told Garvaghy Road protesters that organising or taking part in the protest was an offence liable to arrest and prosecution.
claims.episode_span: the Police Service of Northern Ireland told them that organising or taking part in the protest was an offence liable to arrest and prosecution.
claims.source_title: Orange Order to march down Garvaghy Road for first time in almost 30 years
claims.supporting_quote: Ireland and Britain Editor Mark Hennessy is there now, where demonstrators are being told “organising or taking part in the protest is committing an offence and is liable to arrest and prosecution.”

claims.claim: Five people were killed in incidents linked to the earlier Drumcree tensions.
claims.episode_span: five people were killed in incidents linked to the Drumcree tensions of the 1980s and 1990s.
claims.source_title: Orange Order to march down Garvaghy Road for first time in almost 30 years
claims.supporting_quote: Five people were killed in incidents linked to these tensions.

claims.claim: Poland's defence spending rose from 2.2 percent of GDP to 4.8 percent this year, about 53 billion dollars, fourth in the EU after Germany, France and Italy.
claims.episode_span: Poland's defence spending has risen from 2.2 percent of GDP to 4.8 percent this year, about 53 billion dollars, the fourth-highest cash total in the EU after Germany, France and Italy
claims.source_title: Poland is racing ahead with military spending – but will it help or damage its economic growth story?
claims.supporting_quote: Since Vladimir Putin ordered Russian troops into Ukraine almost five years ago, spending as a share of Polish gross domestic product (GDP ) has more than doubled from 2.2% to 4.8% this year. In cash terms, this equates to $53bn (£39.8bn), the fourth-highest in the EU after Germany, France and Italy.

claims.claim: MBDA Polska opened a weapons facility this month in Czosnów on land that was a cornfield two years ago.
claims.episode_span: in Czosnów, a hi-tech weapons facility that MBDA Polska opened this month stands on ground that was a cornfield two years ago.
claims.source_title: Poland is racing ahead with military spending – but will it help or damage its economic growth story?
claims.supporting_quote: As recently as two years ago, their destination – a hi-tech weapons facility opened this month – had been a cornfield.

claims.claim: Marcin Bosacki said the defence build-up benefits Polish security, defence and the economy and that solidarity and power would discourage Russian attacks on Nato.
claims.episode_span: Deputy foreign minister Marcin Bosacki said the build-up benefits Polish security, defence and the economy, and that solidarity and power are what would discourage attacks on Nato states
claims.source_title: Poland is racing ahead with military spending – but will it help or damage its economic growth story?
claims.supporting_quote: “[It] is clearly benefiting Polish security; Polish defence, and the Polish economy as well,” he says.

claims.claim: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was evicted on a stretcher from a Madrid home she had lived in for seven decades, and The Guardian said an estimated 10,000 people protested in Madrid on Wednesday.
claims.episode_span: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was removed on a stretcher from the Madrid home she had lived in for seven decades
claims.source_title: Eviction of 87-year-old puts Spain’s deepening housing crisis in the spotlight
claims.supporting_quote: Images of an octogenarian being evicted from the home she had lived in for seven decades on a stretcher, flanked by protesters and police officers, sparked indignation across Spain.

claims.claim: Organisers of the Puerta del Sol protest said 300,000 people attended and official numbers were 25,000.
claims.episode_span: organisers said 300,000 people filled the streets and official numbers were 25,000
claims.source_title: Housing anger erupts in Madrid as protesters occupy Sol
claims.supporting_quote: Organizers said 300,000 people filled the streets. Official numbers were much lower—25,000.

claims.claim: Sumar threatened to skip the next Council of Ministers if a housing decree stalls, and Irene Montero said houses are for living and warned that talks with Junts could betray housing campaigners.
claims.episode_span: Sumar threatened to skip the next Council of Ministers if a housing decree stalls, and Podemos leader Irene Montero told marchers the concession this time had to come from rentiers and speculators, because houses are for living.
claims.source_title: Housing anger erupts in Madrid as protesters occupy Sol
claims.supporting_quote: Sumar, the coalition partner, threatened to skip the next Council of Ministers if the housing decree stalls.

claims.claim: RUSSPAIN reported that the Madrid regional government bought a luxury penthouse in Chamberí and that 15,000 people had protested outside that building.
claims.episode_span: the Madrid regional government bought a luxury penthouse in Chamberí, and that 15,000 people had protested outside that building days earlier.
claims.source_title: Housing anger erupts in Madrid as protesters occupy Sol
claims.supporting_quote: The Madrid regional government bought a luxury penthouse in Chamberí. Just days before, 15,000 people protested outside that building.
